name: Legacy Land Conservation Program: Land Acquisition Grant

funder.name: Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources

summary: Competitive Hawaii grants for nonprofit land conservation organisations, counties and State agencies to buy land or conservation easements that protect threatened natural and cultural resources.

eligibility.rule: A nonprofit land conservation organisation, a county or a State agency
Nonprofits: IRS-certified and registered with the Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs
Property has value as a resource to the State for at least one preservation/protection purpose

documents: Agency Consultation Form with agency responses
IRS Nonprofit Determination Letter, if nonprofit applicant
Appraisal or other documentation of estimated fair market value

calls.label: FY2027 land acquisition cycle
calls.note: Date is for the full application; the final application is tentatively due January 2027.

applicant_types.quote: Must be a nonprofit land conservation organization, county, or State agency

geography.quote: acquiring interests in land for protecting Hawaiʻi's most exceptional, unique, threatened, and endangered natural and cultural resources

access.quote: Signing up is the first step

pool.quote: $5.3 million in grant funds is expected to be available for land acquisition grant awards.

co_finance_required.quote: County and nonprofit awardees must provide matching funds that cover at least 25% of total transaction costs.

effort.quote: Agency Consultation Form due to Legacy Land September 14, 2026
The LLCC reviews each application received, including a field visit to each property proposed for conservation.
Applicant presentations to the Commission February 2027 (tentative)

eligibility.quote: Must be a nonprofit land conservation organization, county, or State agency

Nonprofit applicants must be certified by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (see IRS requirements for charities and nonprofits) and registered with the State Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs (see Hawai'i Business Express).
The property to be acquired must have value as a resource to the State for at least one of the following preservation/protection purposes.

co_finance.quote: CAUTION - matching funds for county and nonprofit applicants must be at least 25% of TETC. See Hawaii Administrative Rules section 13-140-20(g). * *** Select C for cash or IK for in-kind.

after_award.quote: Reports on property management using the Monitoring Self-Report form (PDF)
Accommodates site visits for State monitoring of property management

documents.quote: Agency Consultation is a preliminary step in the application process, and the Agency Consultation Form (including agency responses) must be included in your full application.

IRS Nonprofit Determination Letter (required for nonprofit applicants only) IRS favorable determination letter or other evidence of IRS determination/designation of nonprofit status. If the IRS letter is not available, provide a status report with the expected timeline for completion. Mission Statement (required for nonprofit applicants only)
Upload maps and photos of the property to the Maps and Photos subfolder on SharePoint as separate, stand-alone image files, and list them on the Form 1 checklist.
Appraisal or other documentation of Estimated Fair Market Value
